summary: The first half of the week leaned hawkish on data and mixed for stocks. ISM manufacturing beat at 55.5, though prices paid cooled to 75.2, and JOLTS openings jumped to 7.52M, topping every forecast. Apple and Palantir both beat but fell, Apple on its margin outlook, while AMD beat with data center revenue up 97% and rose more than 7% after hours. The S&P 500 slipped Monday, then snapped a three day losing streak Tuesday on a chip rally. Overnight, Democrats were projected to win the House and the Senate, and stock futures fell, led by tech, as the 10 year yield dropped to near 4.91%. Still ahead: ADP, ISM services and the Treasury refunding today along with Qualcomm and Arm after the close, a Bank of England hike on Thursday, and the October jobs report on Friday.

headline.title: Friday Nov 6: the October jobs report at 8:30 AM ET
headline.body: The midterms delivered the expected Democratic wins and tech futures slipped overnight, but payrolls still speak most directly to the Fed's December decision. A strong JOLTS report and a hot factory survey have firmed the hawkish case, so a beat on the 55,000 to 65,000 consensus with firm wages would harden hike bets, while another weak print would give the case for waiting real support.

spotlight.name: Apple
spotlight.when: Mon Nov 2, after the close, call 5:00 PM ET
spotlight.watch: Reported 2.10 versus 1.98 expected and beat on iPhone sales, but guided gross margin to 45% to 46% on high memory chip prices. The stock fell about 1.9% on Tuesday.

spotlight.name: Palantir
spotlight.when: Mon Nov 2, after the close, webcast 5:00 PM ET
spotlight.watch: Reported 0.44 versus 0.39 expected and raised its full year revenue outlook, yet the stock fell as much as 6% early Tuesday before recovering to close down about 1.7%, as analysts flagged slower contract value growth.

spotlight.name: AMD
spotlight.when: Tue Nov 3, after the close, call 5:00 PM ET
spotlight.watch: Reported 2.09 versus 1.89 expected and beat on revenue, with data center revenue up 97%. The stock jumped more than 7% after hours, though overnight election selling in tech futures may trim that at the open.

macro.name: ISM Manufacturing (Oct)
macro.note: Came in at 55.5 versus about 54.6 to 54.7 expected, the tenth straight month of expansion, with production at 59.0, the highest since November 2021. Prices paid eased to 75.2 from 77.9, below the 77 consensus but still high, and employment slipped to 52.4.
macro.react: Stocks split on Monday. The Dow rose about 0.4% as oil posted its sharpest drop in three months on hopes for US and Iran diplomacy, while AI selling pulled the Nasdaq down about 1.1% and the S&P 500 down about 0.5% for a third straight loss.

macro.name: Fed's Goolsbee, Q&A at the BIS
macro.note: The Chicago Fed president is moderating, and is not a voter this year, so this may not carry a policy view.
macro.react: Little market impact is likely unless the comments stray directly onto December.

macro.name: Senior Loan Officer Survey (Q3)
macro.note: Banks reported tighter standards on net for all commercial real estate loan categories and weaker demand for them, a reversal from easing in July. Mortgage demand also weakened while mortgage standards held broadly steady.
macro.react: It was not a market mover. Tighter real estate lending is a modest headwind for regional banks and fits the view that higher rates are starting to bite.

macro.name: Treasury financing estimates
macro.note: Treasury cut its fourth quarter borrowing estimate to $618B, $10B below the August projection, because it started with more cash. Excluding that cushion, the need was $24B higher. It sees $800B of borrowing in the first quarter of 2027.
macro.react: The smaller headline figure eased supply worries going into Wednesday's refunding, and long term yields had no major reaction that day.

macro.name: Reserve Bank of Australia decision
macro.note: The RBA hiked to 4.85% as expected, its fifth hike this year and the highest rate since 2008, but the vote was split 6 to 3 with three members wanting to hold.
macro.react: The split vote read as less hawkish than the hike itself, and some economists now see a December pause as more likely. It added to the global tightening theme without a surprise.

macro.name: US midterm elections
macro.note: Democrats are projected to win the House and, per Fox News Decision Desk, gain control of the Senate, broadly matching prediction market odds. Some close races may still take time to call.
macro.react: Stocks rose Tuesday before results, with the S&P 500 up 0.4% and the Nasdaq up 0.8% on a chip rally. Overnight, futures fell as the sweep came into view, with Nasdaq 100 futures down roughly 0.6% to 2% depending on the time, on worries about AI regulation and limits on data centers. The 10 year yield fell about 6 basis points to near 4.91% and the dollar weakened.

macro.name: JOLTS job openings (Sep)
macro.note: Openings rose to 7.52M versus 7.13M expected, topping every estimate in Bloomberg's survey, and quits jumped by the most since May 2023. August was revised up to 7.2M.
macro.react: It argues the labor market is firmer than recent payrolls suggest, which supports the hawkish case for December heading into Friday. Stock indexes still finished higher on the chip rally.

macro.name: Factory orders (Sep)
macro.note: Orders rose 1.8% versus 1.2% expected, helped by a 28.3% jump in aircraft. Core capital goods orders rose 0.6%.
macro.react: A beat, but mostly known from durable goods, so it did not move markets.

macro.name: Bank of Canada's Macklem at House of Commons committee
macro.note: The governor and senior deputy appear after the recent hike. Markets price about a 55% chance of another in December.
macro.react: A firm tone would lift the Canadian dollar and December odds. Any caution would trim them.

macro.name: Swiss CPI (Oct), Japan closed
macro.note: Swiss inflation comes out at 2:30 AM ET. Tokyo markets are closed for Culture Day.
macro.react: Thin Asian trading can exaggerate moves as election results come in. Swiss CPI mainly matters for the franc.

macro.name: ISM Services (Oct)
macro.note: Services make up most of the US economy, and the survey's prices and employment parts are the details to read ahead of Friday.
macro.react: A beat with hot prices would push yields higher and strengthen December hike bets, a headwind for growth stocks. A softer reading with cooling prices would help tech and small caps, unless it is weak enough to raise growth worries.

macro.name: ADP employment (Oct)
macro.note: A private payrolls preview for Friday, though it is an imperfect guide to the official report.
macro.react: A big beat could firm up payroll expectations and lift yields. A print near zero would add to labor softening concerns and support bonds.

macro.name: Treasury quarterly refunding
macro.cons: Barclays expects no change to auction sizes
macro.note: The Treasury sets auction sizes for the coming quarter, and any change in its guidance matters as much as the sizes themselves.
macro.react: Hints of larger auctions would steepen the curve and hurt rate sensitive stocks. Steady sizes are the expected outcome and should pass quietly.

macro.name: Trade balance (Sep)
macro.note: The gap feeds into revisions to third quarter growth, which came in at 3.4% in the first estimate.
macro.react: A large change could shift GDP revision estimates by a few tenths, but it is rarely a market mover alone.

macro.name: Eurozone flash CPI, Riksbank, Brazil, Poland
macro.cons: Eurozone CPI 3.9% to 4.0%, core 2.2% to 2.5%. Riksbank hike to 2.00%
macro.note: Eurozone inflation rose to 4.0% from 3.8%, at or a tenth above forecasts and the highest since September 2023, driven by energy. The core figure was not confirmed at the time of writing. The Riksbank hiked to 2.00% as expected and signaled more hikes are possible. Brazil and Poland come later, with times varying.
macro.react: Another energy driven jump keeps an ECB hike in December in play, which supports the euro and European yields. Watch whether core stayed steady, since that decides how much of the move is energy alone.

macro.name: Bank of England decision and Monetary Policy Report
macro.prior: 3.75%, 6 to 3 vote to hold in Sep
macro.note: This would start a tightening cycle, and about 98% is priced. Governor Bailey speaks at 7:30 AM ET. Analysts expect pushback against market pricing of more than four hikes over the next 12 months.
macro.react: The hike itself is priced, so the vote split and guidance will drive the reaction. Pushback on the hike path would soften the pound and help gilts and UK stocks. A hawkish vote or no pushback would lift gilt yields and could spill into global bonds.

macro.name: Initial jobless claims
macro.note: The four week average is 197,800, a very low level that sits oddly next to weak payroll growth.
macro.react: Another reading under 200,000 keeps the low firing story and the hawkish case alive. A jump above 220,000 would be a real change, helping bonds and weakening December hike odds.

macro.name: Productivity and unit labor costs (Q3)
macro.note: With strong growth and little hiring, productivity may look solid. Unit labor costs are the inflation angle.
macro.react: Strong productivity with tame labor costs supports the AI productivity story and is friendly for stocks. A jump in unit labor costs would add to inflation worries and push yields up.

macro.name: Fed's Hammack
macro.note: The Cleveland Fed president dissented in favor of a hike last week, so this is an early look at the hawkish case.
macro.react: Hawkish comments are expected. Only a clear push for a larger move or a softening of the view would surprise markets.

macro.name: Challenger job cuts (Oct)
macro.note: Announced layoffs, with technology accounting for 10,800 in September.
macro.react: A large rise, especially in tech, would feed labor softening concerns ahead of Friday. Otherwise it is background.

macro.name: Norges Bank, Czech National Bank, Banxico, Canada budget, Lagarde
macro.cons: Norges hold at 4.50%, Czech hike to 4.00%, Banxico hold at 6.50%
macro.note: Norges Bank is at 4:00 AM ET and ECB President Lagarde speaks at 11:00 AM ET. Other times vary. Japan also auctions 10 year bonds and publishes Bank of Japan minutes.
macro.react: These mostly move their own currencies. A weak Japanese bond auction could push global long term yields higher, which matters most for US growth stocks.

macro.name: October jobs report
macro.cons: Payrolls 55,000 to 65,000. Unemployment 4.2%. Hourly earnings +0.3% m/m, 2.9% y/y
macro.prior: Payrolls 29,000. Unemployment 4.2%. Hourly earnings +0.1% m/m, 3.0% y/y
macro.note: September missed badly and prior months were revised down by 60,000 in total. The three month average is about 50,700. Watch revisions and wages as closely as the headline.
macro.react: A strong number with firm wages would nearly lock in a December hike: yields and the dollar up, tech and small caps down, banks more resilient. A negative or very weak number would pull hike odds down and rally bonds, though stocks could stumble if it raises growth fears. An in line report is largely priced, so a muted move is the likeliest outcome.

macro.name: University of Michigan sentiment, preliminary (Nov)
macro.note: Sentiment is very low. The inflation expectations figure is what the Fed will watch.
macro.react: A rise in expectations above 4.7% would add to hawkish pressure and lift yields. A decline would be welcome relief for bonds, and any post election swing in sentiment should be read cautiously.

macro.name: Fed speakers Williams, Musalem, Bowman
macro.note: Williams speaks at 4:30 AM ET, Musalem at 9:10 AM ET and Bowman at 12:15 PM ET. Musalem and Bowman get the first word after the jobs report.
macro.react: Williams carries the most weight as a permanent voter, so any comment on December could move rates. Comments after payrolls could either confirm or fade the market's first reaction.

macro.name: Canada jobs, eurozone retail sales, BoJ's Ueda
macro.note: Canada reports at 8:30 AM ET, eurozone sales at 5:00 AM ET, and Ueda gives an IMF lecture at 11:00 AM ET.
macro.react: Another poor Canadian report would cut December hike odds there, about 55% now, and weaken the Canadian dollar. A hawkish Ueda would support the yen and could pressure carry trades.

notes: Earnings shows large market cap names and widely traded movers, not every report. EPS figures are consensus estimates from Robinhood data and can differ from other sources. Reported figures are adjusted EPS from the same data. Lumentum moved to Monday morning after reporting early. Names without a confirmed timing, such as DoorDash and Berkshire Hathaway, are left out.

Consensus figures come from public week ahead previews and can change. Where sources differ, a range is shown. Apple's revenue figure is a range implied by its growth guidance, not a consensus. Palantir and AMD revenue are from public previews. Implied earnings moves are not included.
Reaction notes are scenario thinking, not predictions.
